name: nanovm
description: Micro-VMs out of nothing but the Linux kernel — a fully open-source (MIT) nanovm framework in pure Go, zero dependencies, one static binary. A nanovm is a process behind its own PID/UTS/mount/IPC (and optionally net) namespaces, its own root filesystem via pivot_root, and a cgroup v2 slice for memory, cpu and pid caps. The default boot is a read-only lens over the host with a private /proc and /tmp, so it is useful with zero setup; point rootfs at any directory (the busybox helper, a docker export, debootstrap) to pivot into a real root. No daemon, no image format, no C: library + CLI + HTTP API + web console, all one binary you can read end to end.

endpoints./info: Null call — what this module is and what it exposes
endpoints./health: Liveness and a vm count; says so when the server is down
endpoints./vms: GET every vm (liveness refreshed) · POST a Spec to boot one, always detached
endpoints./vms/{name}: GET one vm's state · DELETE stops and forgets it
endpoints./vms/{name}/stop: POST — SIGTERM pid 1 of the namespace, SIGKILL after 3s
endpoints./vms/{name}/exec: POST {cmd:[...]} — run inside via nsenter, output captured
endpoints./vms/{name}/logs: GET the last lines of a detached vm (?tail=100)

notes.open_source: MIT, pure Go standard library — no modules downloaded, no C, no Docker; the whole runtime is ~1000 lines in src/
notes.isolation: namespaces + pivot_root + cgroup v2, not hardware virtualization — same tier as containers, not KVM; a kernel exploit escapes it
notes.root: creating namespaces and cgroup slices needs root (or CAP_SYS_ADMIN); the fleet runs as root so this is moot here
notes.exec: entering a running vm uses util-linux nsenter — setns(CLONE_NEWNS) refuses multithreaded callers, which every Go process is
notes.meminfo: /proc/meminfo inside a vm shows host totals (it is not cgroup-aware); the cap is real — the OOM killer answers at memory.max
notes.state: ~/.mod/nanovm — one JSON per vm, logs for detached ones; NANOVM_DATA overrides for tests
